name: Archer Draw Isometric Hold
description: Band-simulated full-draw isometric hold — builds the upper-back endurance specific to archery anchor position.
instructions_excerpt: Stand tall with a resistance band in the draw hand and the other arm extended toward the imaginary target. Draw the band to the anchor position (side of face/under chin). Hold the full-draw position 15-30 seconds.

name: Archer Pull-Up
description: Asymmetric pull-up — one arm does most of the work while the other extends to the side.
instructions_excerpt: Grip the bar wide. Pull up toward one hand while the other arm stays extended and braces against the bar. Chin clears the bar near the working hand. Lower under control. Alternate sides.

name: Archery Draw-Hold Isometric
description: Band-draw-and-hold isometric — archery-specific draw endurance.
instructions_excerpt: Band anchored at chest height in front. Draw to full archer position (anchor at jaw), hold 10-20s. 4-6 reps.

name: Campus Board Ladder (1-3-5)
description: Max-effort contact strength on a campus board — reserved for advanced climbers.
instructions_excerpt: Fully warm up: dynamic shoulder mobility + easy climbing + sub-max hangs. On a campus board with evenly-spaced rungs, start matched on rung 1. Move the leading hand up to rung 3, then the trailing hand to rung 5. Reverse down. Rest 3 minutes between reps. 3-5 reps is a full session.

name: Dead Hang with Pack
description: Dead hang wearing a light pack — grip and shoulder endurance for alpine/via-ferrata objectives.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from a pull-up bar wearing a light pack. Full hang, shoulders engaged. Hold 15-45s. Build duration before adding load.

name: Dynamic Lock-Off (Campus-Lite)
description: Pull-up + lock-off + controlled release — builds contact strength.
instructions_excerpt: From a pull-up bar, pull into a chest-to-bar position, hold 2s, release one hand to a briefly lower position before re-catching. Alternate sides. Build to deeper releases over weeks.

name: Fat-Grip Dead Hang
description: Thick-bar dead hang — forearm and grip endurance closer to the grip demands of a gi sleeve or wrist.
instructions_excerpt: Wrap a thick-grip attachment around a pull-up bar (or hang on a 2.5"+ bar). Hang with shoulders engaged. Target 20-45 seconds. Rest fully between sets.

name: Finger Extensor Band Work (Rice Bucket Alt)
description: Forearm extensor activation for finger openers — the climber prehab staple.
instructions_excerpt: Loop a light rubber band over the fingertips of one hand with fingers bunched together in a cup. Open the fingers wide, extending against the band. Close slowly. Start with 25-40 reps per hand.

name: Front Lever Progression (Tuck / Advanced Tuck)
description: Straight-body hold parallel to the ground — core + pulling integration.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings. Pull your knees to chest into a tuck, then lift hips and tilt back until torso and bent legs are horizontal. Hold the tuck for 5-15 seconds with lats engaged pulling the bar toward hips. Progress by extending legs (advanced tuck → one-leg → straddle → full).

name: Half-Kneeling Archer Band Pull
description: Half-kneeling horizontal row with one-arm anchored — scap retraction + anti-rotation for boxers and grapplers whose posture collapses forward.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor a band at chest height. Take a half-kneeling stance facing the anchor. Hold the band with both hands, arms extended. Keep one arm long while the other rows back with elbow close to the ribs, squeezing the shoulder blade. Alternate sides each set.

name: Hangboard Max Hang (20mm Edge)
description: Near-max isometric dead hang on a 20mm edge — the benchmark for finger strength.
instructions_excerpt: After a thorough warm-up including 3-4 sub-maximal hangs, hang from a 20mm edge with a half-crimp or open-hand grip (never full crimp). Target hangs of 7-10 seconds at an intensity where you could hold 2-3 more seconds at most. Add weight via harness if bodyweight is too easy. Rest 2-3 minutes betwe

name: Hangboard Repeaters (7/3 Protocol)
description: Strength-endurance protocol on a 20mm edge — six-set hang block.
instructions_excerpt: On a 20mm edge, hang for 7 seconds, rest 3 seconds, repeat for 6 hangs = one set. Rest 2-3 minutes between sets. Do 3-6 sets. Intensity: by hang 6 you should feel you have 1-2 more hangs in the tank. Use the same half-crimp or open-hand grip throughout; do not switch grips mid-set.

name: Hangboard Repeaters (Endurance Variant)
description: Sub-maximal long repeater protocol — finger endurance for sport/trad.
instructions_excerpt: On a 20mm edge or larger, hang for 10 seconds / rest 5 seconds, repeat for 6 hangs = one set. Rest 1 minute between sets. Do 4-6 sets. Intensity should stay sub-maximal — you could do 2 more hangs at the end of each set.

name: Ice Tool Dead Hang (Tool-Grip Sim)
description: Dead hang on an ice tool or grip-sim attachment — the direct transfer to hooked/ice grip endurance.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from ice tools mounted to a pull-up bar, or from a grip-bar simulating a D-shaped ice-tool handle. 15-45s. Shoulders engaged.

name: Lock-Off Hold (90°)
description: Isometric elbow-flexed hold at 90° — direct transfer to static climbing moves.
instructions_excerpt: From a pull-up bar, pull up to a position where your elbows are bent 90° and chin is at bar height. Hold for 5-10 seconds with shoulders engaged and core tight. Lower under control. Progress by adding weight or by holding one-armed on the off-hand.

name: Low-Row Isometric (Archery Posture)
description: Rowed isometric with light band — prehab for archery / bow hunting upper-back endurance.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor band at chest height. Grip and row elbows past the ribs. Hold 20-30s. Keep mid-back squeezed.

name: One-Arm Hang (Assisted)
description: One-arm dead hang with pulley or band assist — builds asymmetric finger strength.
instructions_excerpt: Use a pulley-and-counterweight system or a large resistance band looped over the bar for assist. Start with ~30-40% bodyweight of assistance and reduce over weeks. Hang on one arm from a 20mm edge or jug for 5-10 seconds, shoulder engaged. Alternate arms. Always use the assist until comfortable with

name: Open-Hand Dead Hang
description: Pulley-friendly open-hand hang — prehab + general finger conditioning.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from a pull-up bar or jug with an open-hand grip (fingers together, NOT crimped). Shoulders actively engaged (not shrugged). Hold for 20-40 seconds. Rest 60 seconds between sets.

name: Rappel Brake-Hand Isometric
description: Heavy band pull-down held static with one hand — builds the brake-hand strength for long rappels.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor a heavy band overhead. Grip with one hand. Pull down to the hip and hold 15-30s, arm bent just past 90. Keep scapula packed. Switch sides.

name: Rice Bucket Training
description: Full forearm conditioning via resistive grip movements in a bucket of rice.
instructions_excerpt: Fill a deep bucket with uncooked rice. Plunge your hand into the rice and perform 30-45 seconds of varied movements: fist-clench/release, finger spread, wrist rotation, dig + claw, forearm twist. Switch hands.

name: Theraputty / Finger Flexor Isolation
description: Graded-resistance finger flexor work — ideal post-pulley rehab.
instructions_excerpt: Use a color-graded theraputty (soft to firm). Squeeze, pinch, and open the putty with the affected hand through a set of controlled finger movements for 60-90 seconds. Progress putty firmness over weeks.

name: Typewriter Pull-Up
description: Advanced pulling drill — pull to one side, shift across, lower.
instructions_excerpt: From a pull-up bar, perform a pull-up and hold at the top with chin over bar. Shift your body laterally to bring your chin over one hand; pause. Shift across to the other hand; pause. Lower under control. This is one rep.

name: Via Ferrata Arm-Over-Arm Cable Sim
description: Hand-over-hand rope/band climb simulation — specific to via-ferrata cable-handling endurance.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor a thick rope or heavy band overhead at an angle. Climb hand-over-hand along it for 4-8 m, step back, repeat. 4-6 rounds.

name: Via Ferrata Cable-Pull Simulation
description: Vertical band pull + hand-over-hand simulation — mimics the via-ferrata cable clip-and-pull rhythm.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor a heavy band high. Stand below. Pull the band toward you hand-over-hand in a controlled rhythm, alternating hands just like clipping past anchors. 30-45s sets.
